body:
# Exact source-owned connection goal component

Parent: ladon-real-prose-contracts Task 2.2 (open, 4/6). Separate engineering component; the old 600-second feasibility clock is closed. This component introduces no public producer, native connection or semantic admission.

Build a new additive Lean constructor, leaving correspondence_check._check_goal and real_bound_admission_worker._accepted unchanged. Its one target is formalType -> premise1 -> ... -> premiseN -> authoredValue. Each owner must be local to the current copied module, have an exact selected declaration range, an exact bounded typed expression, a required declaration kind (formal theorem, authored/premise Prop definitions), and no escaping variables/metavariables. Preserve actual Expr binder names; only the comparison view may erase binder names. Formal type uses existing zeta-normalized observation view; authored/premises use exact definition values. Reject imported, kind, range, module, expression, duplicate-owner and malformed request substitutions. At most 16 ordered premises; renderer 100000 nodes/depth128, request/output8MiB. Kernel completion/replay remains separate and mandatory. Existing capture/completion own copied source/import/toolchain custody; this component alone makes no claim about original-to-copy mapping or fresh formal admission.

Red tests must fail for missing component behavior, then remain frozen. Generic Lean controls must demonstrate exact goal with all ordered premises, actual capture/completion accepted with standard-axiom trust, and rejection of owner mutations. No target-specific names, losses, carriers, Quux import, packages, caches or cap changes. Root owns edits/builds/tests/board. Workers read only or write ignored scratch proposals. Existing dirty tree is preserved, no commit/push. Component budget: each supervised operation <=600s, 12GiB process-tree RSS, 8MiB output; informed requalification is a later separate gate, not a restart of the old probe.

author: /root/exact_goal_red_65
body: Proposed decisive generic red tests (no test edits or runs): (1) A generic formal theorem plus authored Prop definition and two ordered premise Prop definitions constructs exactly formalType -> premise1 -> premise2 -> authoredValue; ensure order matters by making reverse order fail at typechecking. (2) Reject each single-owner mutation independently: formal owner changed to a local definition, authored owner changed to a theorem, premise owner changed to theorem/non-Prop def, declaration moved outside the selected exact range, same-named declaration imported instead of locally declared, owner source/module switched, owner expression changed while range stays, duplicate owner ID, swapped formal/authored role, omitted/reordered premise, and malformed/unknown request field. (3) Reject expressions with free fvars or expr/level metavariables; reject >16 premises and renderer boundary inputs at >100000 nodes, depth>128, and request/output >8MiB; accept at exactly each stated ceiling when otherwise valid. (4) Ensure preserved Expr binder names appear in constructed telescope while only comparison projection erases names; a name substitution in a comparison-only case should compare equal, but must not rewrite stored/output Expr. (5) Distinguish formal-type observation normalization from authored/premise exact values: a zeta-only formal observation case may pass; changing the authored or premise value must fail even if type remains Prop. Generic completion control must separately prove/replay accepted with only allowed standard axioms; constructor acceptance alone is not proof evidence. These are proposed red cases, not executed tests.

body: Authority/schema risks: request-supplied names/ranges/Expr JSON are claims, not authority; resolve owners only in the current helper's exact copied-module environment and bind each role to the validated local declaration plus exact selected byte range. Reject imported declarations even when fully qualified/name/type match; reject forged range aliases and ambiguous duplicate identity. Keep module/source digest, capture contextRef, selected syntax range and declaration identity joined through constructor input validation; this component does not re-establish original-to-copy or import custody, so rely on capture/completion's existing checks and do not claim admission. Use closed exact request/object schemas, strict JSON scalar typing (bool must not pass integer checks), canonical bounded Expr parsing, duplicate-key rejection, safe node/depth accounting before allocation, and explicit per-premise ordered list (not map); cap ordered premises at 16. Check Expr no escaping FVars/expr MVars/level MVars and no untrusted binder-name rewrite. Check formal declaration is theorem and formal expression matches zeta-normalized observed type; authored/premise owners are local Prop definitions whose exact values match; do not accept mere Prop type or name match. Existing source observation validates an exact single goal context/import closure/toolchain; completion freshly re-captures, validates context/import inventory, replays and checks allowed axioms; keep that separate kernel gate intact. Inspected: .codex/state/real-prose-exact-goal/CONTRACT.md; openspec/changes/ladon-real-prose-contracts/evidence/exact-connection-feasibility-20261027/REPORT.md; src/ladon/_source_goal_protocol.py; src/ladon/source_goal_capture.py; src/ladon/source_goal_completion.py; existing tests/test_source_goal_* inventory. author: /root/exact_goal_audit_66
body:
Independent read-only audit of src/ladon/lean/LadonProseExactGoal.lean, frozen contract, and both exact-goal test files. No source/test edits; no tests, Lean builds, or shared builds run (root owns these).

Finding: the 8 MiB output bound is not enforced. The macro checks request bytes at lines 135-137 and expression node/depth limits in renderNode, but there is no serialized rendered-JSON byte-size check after rendering owner expressions (lines 129-130) or the assembled target (line 169). A request near 8 MiB can contain large expression payloads and the constructed telescope adds generated forall wrappers; bounded nodes/depth alone does not enforce an output-byte ceiling. Add a byte-size check against canonical serialized rendered JSON before accepting each renderer result (including the final target), or narrow the contract if this limit is not intended for this internal projection. Existing tests exercise deep-expression and premise-count limits but not request/output byte boundaries.

Otherwise, source inspection found the main ownership checks coherent with contract: local declaration/module lookup, exact full/selection range, required theorem/Prop-definition info, exact Expr comparison with formal-only zeta reduction, closure checks, explicit ordered premises and duplicate-owner rejection. Constructed target uses original Expr values, so erased binder names in JSON comparison do not rename stored binders; tests inspect this directly. This is source review only, not runtime assurance.
